_comment: 🧩️ This subset's contribution to the repository test platform — the BMP v3 ✳️any mutation catalog and its dedicated mutate oracle. Discovered by convention (`testContributionDirName` in 🔣️taxonomy.json); the shared stdio manifest (`✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio/🔣️oracle.json`) already registers `image-bmp` under capability `bmp-raster` for plain create/round-trip coverage — mutation coverage needs its own capability so the two are never conflated, per the wave-7 fleet brief.

oracles.rationale:
🫥️ RECLASSIFIED. The third-party crate here does REAL codec work — it decodes the artifact and will reject a malformed one — but that is not what the mutation test turns on. What the OUTPUT OF A MUTATION SHOULD BE is computed by this owner's own `🦀️oracle.rs`, whose `apply_kind` dispatch is a second implementation of this subset's mutation semantics. Its own doc comment says so: it "deliberately mirrors" the production `diff` rather than diverging from it. Both halves of the comparison therefore read the same specification, and a misreading of it produces two agreeing wrong answers.

The honest split is that the crate discharges "the result is a well-formed file of this format", and NOT "the mutation computed the right answer". Only the second is what a mutation oracle is for, so this is a `cross-semio-implementation`: a required SUPPLEMENT, never a substitute. A qualifying third-party reference for the mutation semantics is still owed.

productionDebt.plan: The `image` crate is production-reachable TODAY from two places: the 🎞️animate plugin's video engine and 🧰️framework/🔨️modules/🗺️surface's tiled-map. Discovered by the oracle-purity gate the moment `image` was registered — the gate did its job. Phase 7 target: both call sites want raster decode/encode that ✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio already implements, so routing them through decode_bmp / decode_tiff / decode_jpg retires the dependency and this record with it.

oracles.rationale:
📖️ A READER, and that is the whole point of registering it separately from `image-bmp-3-mutate` above.

That sibling entry is `cross-semio-implementation`: what a mutation SHOULD produce is computed by this owner's own `🦀️oracle.rs` (533 lines, whose own header states it 'deliberately mirrors' the production diff semantics), so both halves of that comparison descend from one reading of the format's specification.

This entry is a different mechanism. The expected state is not computed at all — it is COMMITTED, as the `after` half of a byte-reproducible fixture built directly by the standalone `image-bmp-codec` binary (`../🏭️generator/🦀️image-bmp-codec`, depends on nothing but `image` 0.25's own `bmp` feature). `image` then decodes BOTH sides through its own public `BmpDecoder`/`BmpEncoder` surface, and the comparison is over what it recovered — no BITMAPINFOHEADER byte-offset parsing of this module's own, unlike the sibling `component.rs`. The probes say so in their own header: 'Everything here MARSHALS and READS; nothing here applies a mutation or predicts what one should.'

Only 4 of this subset's 5 declared `bmp-3-mutate` kinds are registered against this oracle. `change-header-fields` is not: reading `image-0.25.10`'s own vendored decoder/encoder source (`src/codecs/bmp/{decoder,encoder}.rs`) shows `BmpDecoder`'s `top_down`, `bit_count` and `colors_used` fields are private with no public accessor, and `BmpEncoder::encode_with_palette` hard-codes horizontal/vertical pixels-per-metre to `0`, 'colours important' to `0`, colour planes to `1`, compression to 'none', and always stores rows bottom-up — none of `change-header-fields`' twelve payload fields (`rowOrder`, `xPixelsPerMeter`, `yPixelsPerMeter`, `compression`, `colorsUsed` as a value distinct from palette length, `colorsImportant`, `headerSize`, `imageSize`, an exact `bitsPerPixel`) round-trips through `image`'s public BMP API in either direction. Only `width`/`height` do (via `BmpDecoder::dimensions`), and this subset's own committed production test scenario for `change-header-fields` (`../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/📐️change-header-fields/🧪️tests/direct-behavior/🦠️mutation/🔣️.json`) exercises `width` paired with `xPixelsPerMeter`/`yPixelsPerMeter` together — exactly the fields this reader cannot see — so a width-only recipe would dodge the mutation's own real target fields rather than honestly witness it. See `oracleRequirements` below and the `bmp-3-mutate-uncarried` capability, and this subset's own `📓️bmp-v3-any-reader-oracle-retrofit.md` for the full source-level evidence trail.

`productionReachable` is `false`: every non-test/non-scratch `Cargo.toml` in this repository that depends on `image` (`🎞️animate`, `🖍️draw`, `🧰️framework/🔨️modules/🗺️surface`, `🧰️framework/🛍️products/💻️os/🔨️modules/♾️infinite`, and the os renderer's wgpu target) enables only `png`/`jpeg`/`webp`/`gif` — none enables the `bmp` feature `image`'s BMP codec is gated behind. The only Cargo.toml in this repository enabling `image`'s `bmp` feature outside a scratch ticket directory is `✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio/🧪️oracle/📦️packages/🦀️rust/Cargo.toml` itself, an `optional = true` dependency of the shared test-oracle host crate. `image`'s BMP support is therefore genuinely test-only in this repository today, which is a narrower claim than the sibling `image-bmp-3-mutate` entry's own `productionReachable: true` (with a `productionDebt` naming `🎞️animate`'s video engine and `🧰️framework/🔨️modules/🗺️surface`'s tiled-map as reachable-from sites) — that claim is about the `image` package as a whole being production-reachable for OTHER formats it does compile in for (png/jpeg/webp/gif), not about its BMP codec specifically, which is what this entry's capability is scoped to. Left as-is per this ticket's scope (leave `image-bmp-3-mutate` untouched); flagged here as a real, source-verified discrepancy rather than silently copied.

📖️ A SECOND reader, at the HEADER level the first one decodes past.

`image`-rs decodes a BMP to PIXELS: the BITMAPINFOHEADER's resolution fields and colour-table bookkeeping are consumed on the way and never surfaced, so `change-header-fields` was `-uncarried` against it. Honest about `image`, and not a claim about BMP readers.

Pillow both WRITES those fields — `dpi=` sets `biXPelsPerMeter`/`biYPelsPerMeter`, measured as 3780 against 11811 — and READS them back. The projection unpacks the header's whole fixed layout (width, height, planes, bits-per-pixel, compression, image size, both resolution axes, colours used and colours important), so a change to any of the ten is a difference, not just the two this fixture happens to move.

comparisonProfiles.description: BMP v3 documents compared structurally through `image`'s own public decode surface: width, height, storage kind ('indexed' or 'direct'), the full palette table as `image`'s own `get_palette()` returns it (always 256 zero-padded `{r,g,b}` entries for an indexed file, `null` for a direct-colour one — kept as real typed values, never digested, so a diff names the exact entry and channel a palette mutation touched), and the pixel payload (the raw index buffer for an indexed file, the resolved RGB buffer for a direct-colour one) as a size+digest pair, since the committed fixture's own pixel data can run into the thousands of bytes and the comparison engine would otherwise be diffing raw hex. Arrays are order-significant: palette-entry position is semantic identity for `insert-palette-entry`/`remove-palette-entry`, which shift every entry after the touched index rather than being reordered before comparison.

The whole fixed BITMAPINFOHEADER layout — width, height, planes, bits-per-pixel, compression, image size, both pixels-per-metre axes, colours used and colours important — plus mode and size as anchors.

probes.rationale: An INDEPENDENT reader (image's own public BmpDecoder, via the standalone image-bmp-codec binary) accepts both files at all. Nothing downstream means anything if one of them does not decode.

qualification.evidence: Run against every one of this session's 4 generated recipes (8 files) — bothImport true in every case; confirmed directly for insert-palette-entry-applied/{before,after}.bmp.

criteria.detail: decodes width/height, an indexed file's own 256-entry palette table plus raw index buffer, or a direct-colour file's resolved RGB buffer
image-bmp-codec depends only on image 0.25.10 (bmp feature only), resolved from the local cargo registry cache; no network during execution

probes.rationale: The typed projection semantic-bmp-reader-v1 is measured against — width, height, storage kind, the full 256-entry palette table (indexed) or null (direct), and the pixel/index payload as size+digest.

qualification.evidence: Run against replace-pixel-data-applied/after.bmp: reports storage "direct", width 4, height 4, paletteEntries 0, pixels {size:48, digest:"sha256:8917afc0…"}. Run against insert-palette-entry-applied/before.bmp: reports storage "indexed", paletteEntries 256 (image's own get_palette() zero-pads to 256 regardless of the 7 real entries the recipe wrote), with the 7 real colours present at indices 0-6.

criteria.detail: an indexed file's palette+indices project separately from a direct-colour file's resolved pixel buffer, so a palette-only mutation (indices untouched) is distinguishable from a pixel-data mutation
the index/pixel buffer projects as size+digest; the palette table stays a real typed {r,g,b} array so a diff names the exact entry and channel

probes.rationale: Ordered structural equality over two independently-decoded projections — the GATING comparison. Computes no mutation semantics, only structural equality of two already-existing byte blobs.

qualification.evidence: Validated BOTH ways this session with real measured numbers, for all 4 fixtures. Accept: every fixture's own before.bmp compared against itself -> {equal:true, diffCount:0}. Reject, with the diff naming the exact field: replace-palette-entry-applied's before.bmp vs after.bmp -> {equal:false, diffCount:3, diffs:["$.palette[5].r: 0 ≠ 200","$.palette[5].g: 0 ≠ 150","$.palette[5].b: 0 ≠ 100"]}; replace-pixel-data-applied's before.bmp vs after.bmp -> {equal:false, diffCount:1, diffs:["$.pixels.digest: … ≠ …"]}. A first version of the remove-palette-entry-applied recipe (six palette entries, the removed one last) round-tripped to equal:true/diffCount:0 — a false pass, because image's get_palette() always zero-pads to 256 entries so shifting only padding into the removed slot is invisible; the recipe was corrected to carry a second, non-zero spare entry after the removed one, and now measures {equal:false, diffCount:6} with the diff naming positions 5 and 6.

criteria.detail: identical before/after bytes compare equal:true, diffCount:0, for all 4 fixtures
each fixture's real before/after pair compares equal:false with diffs naming the exact field(s); the palette zero-padding trap above was caught by this exact check, not assumed away

qualification.evidence: Validated BOTH ways: (before,before) -> equal:true; (before,after) -> equal:false, on biXPelsPerMeter/biYPelsPerMeter moving 3780 -> 11811. Observability is also enforced at generation time. The projection covers all ten BITMAPINFOHEADER fields rather than only the pair this fixture moves, so it does not silently narrow to what was tested.
